title: Streetwear landing page with oversized headlines, cut-out hero and a 'rotate your phone' prompt
attribution_visible_in_image: Visible brand 'VYBE' and 'The Vybe Tribe' (mockup brand). No creator credit visible.

observed.layout: A landscape website mockup shown rotated 90 degrees inside a portrait frame, with a small rotate icon and the text 'Rotate your phone please :)' on the left. In the landscape layout: vertical nav (Shop, Collections, About, Contact), 'VYBE' logo, oversized black condensed headlines 'Own the EDGE' and 'Keep the VIBE' placed around a cut-out model who overlaps a coral panel. The panel contains 'New Arrivals', 'Where Art Meets your Style', a sentence of body copy, a white 'New Drops' pill with an arrow, a 'Rated 5 Stars by The Vybe Tribe' pill with avatars, three small feature labels (Unique Designs, Limited Drops, Future Threads), and a Featured Product card (photo, 'Urban Vanguard Tee', $26.72 price pill). A cart pill reads '1 product'. Pink brush swirls sit behind the model.
observed.hierarchy: Oversized headlines, then the cut-out subject, then the panel copy and CTA.
observed.typography: Heavy condensed display sans for headlines; clean sans for body. Unconfirmed.
observed.materials: Flat coral panel with a cut-out photo breaking its edge; translucent pill overlays.

interpretation.aesthetic: Loud streetwear brand site; attitude carried by type scale and a subject that breaks the panel.
implementation_notes: Cut-out photo as a transparent PNG layered over the panel with a higher z-index.
Headlines positioned around the subject; text-behind-subject effects need a separate cut-out layer.
The rotate prompt suggests the layout is landscape-only rather than responsive.

concept_work.essence: Brand attitude through scale: huge type, a subject that escapes its container, and one bright field.
what_makes_it_work: A direct purchase path through the featured product card.
gaps_to_make_it_work: White text on coral measures about 2.8:1, including the large sub-head.
The layout depends on landscape, so phone users are told to rotate instead of getting a responsive layout.
Feature labels and body text are very small on coral.

components.name: Cut-out hero photo
components.role: focal point; breaks the panel edge

shared_tokens: coral as the single brand color
pill shapes for every action and badge
links: Headlines wrap the subject so type and photo read as one composition.
'New Arrivals' and 'New Drops' label and action repeat the same idea.
The price pill reuses the panel's coral so the product card belongs to the panel.

approach: Layered divs with a transparent cut-out image
Responsive restack: headlines above the subject on narrow screens
Real orientation-independent layout instead of a rotate prompt

pattern.name: Type-around-subject hero with cut-out overlap
use_when: Fashion, streetwear or youth brands that need attitude
avoid_when: Text must remain readable over imagery without a scrim
must_preserve: Headline contrast against its own background
adaptation_examples: Sneaker drop: shoe cut-out, headlines vertical, price pill kept.
Music festival: performer cut-out, ticket CTA pill.

lessons: Make a layout respond to the viewport instead of asking the user to rotate the device.
Large type does not remove the need for contrast: check text on brand colors.

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
palette: red, teal-green and blue from the garment (saturated medians)
measured.color_roles: Coral as the single brand field; black for headlines; white for text on coral and for UI surfaces.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: A fashion drop site with a clear purchase path.
Strong scale contrast, depth and a single brand color.
Landing conventions are present, but forcing landscape instead of responding to the viewport is a web-correctness problem, and text contrast is low.
Phone users must rotate; small labels; only the default state is shown.
Pills, radii and color are used consistently.
Oversized type around a panel-breaking subject is distinctive.
Scored on conservative values: primary text min 2.79:1; secondary text min 2.78:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

critical_failures.description: A primary text/label measures below 3:1 contrast (best estimate)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
